The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2021> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168314>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

# Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed here, at render time, from
# the output the maintained rewrite writes. Nothing is typed. That includes numbers
# that were not wrong: a token carried over from the published sentence is otherwise
# inherited on trust rather than verified.
out <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)

design <- out("text_design_parameters.csv")
descriptive <- out("text_descriptive_claims.csv")
block_ates <- out("figure_3_blocked_block_ates.csv")
facets <- out("figure_3_blocked_facets_estimates.csv")

param <- function(fig, q) {
  v <- design$value[design$figure == fig & design$quantity == q]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v
}

target <- function(fig, q) {
  v <- descriptive$value[descriptive$figure == fig & descriptive$quantity == q]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v
}

block_ate <- function(n) {
  v <- block_ates$estimate[block_ates$neighborhood == n]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  # An en dash for the minus sign, matching the chapter's own typesetting.
  str_replace(sprintf("%.2f", v), "^-", "--")
}

block_mean <- function(n, cond) {
  v <- facets$estimate[facets$panel == "Faceted by block" &
                         facets$block == paste("Neighborhood", n) &
                         facets$condition == cond]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  sprintf("%.2f", v)
}

# The chapter writes its ranges with an en dash; the pipeline writes "a to b".
en_range <- function(s) str_replace(s, " to ", "--")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file, which is what any other document carrying these corrections reads. Before the
# spine existed an entry was written out in prose wherever it was needed, and the copies
# had already diverged.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be set by any of them.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# A published or corrected value that the pipeline computes stays computed: the field is
# built with str_glue() so the number is produced when this document renders, not typed.
#
# claim_ids is the semicolon-separated list of ground-truth claim_id values the entry
# corrects, and it is what makes "is this finding published?" a query rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where an entry has no ground-truth row, which is normal for a
# bibliographic or structural entry. ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R refuses to build if
# any id here is absent from the ground truth.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. Each value comes from the same expression
# that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks
# that each one is still inside the span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity carries NA, and so does a note-form entry, which corrects nothing.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "description", "pipeline", "full",
  "The two neighborhoods are transposed in the discussion of Figure 17.3",
  "p. 328, Section 17.5.2",
  "In Figure 17.3a, we facet by block. Within each facet, the groups that are compared are formed by random assignment: we see small effects of treatment in neighborhood [[1]] and large negative effects of treatment in neighborhood [[2]].",
  "In Figure 17.3a, we facet by block. Within each facet, the groups that are compared are formed by random assignment: we see small effects of treatment in neighborhood [[2]] and large negative effects of treatment in neighborhood [[1]].",
  str_glue(
    "The large negative effect is in neighborhood 1, where the treated mean is ",
    "{block_mean(1, 'Treatment')} against a control mean of {block_mean(1, 'Control')}, an ",
    "effect of {block_ate(1)}. In neighborhood 2 the effect is {block_ate(2)}. Figure 17.3 ",
    "itself is right: its left facet is labelled \"Neighborhood 1\" and shows the drop, and ",
    "the deposited data generator writes the effect as `-4 * Z * (neighborhood == 1)`. Only ",
    "the sentence describing the figure is wrong."),
  "fig3_block_effects",
  NA_character_,

  2, "definition", "pipeline", "full",
  "The clustered outcome is not confined to the scale the chapter states",
  "p. 329, Section 17.5.3",
  "In this example, we imagine a \"test-prep\" treatment that is randomly assigned to some classrooms but not to others; the outcome is measured on a [[400--1600]]-point scale.",
  str_glue("In this example, we imagine a \"test-prep\" treatment that is randomly assigned to some classrooms but not to others; the outcome is measured on a [[{en_range(param('Figure 17.4', 'Outcome range'))}]]-point scale."),
  str_glue(
    "The example intends the SAT scale, and the deposited generator does not enforce it: it ",
    "draws a classroom shock and a student shock from unbounded normal distributions, so ",
    "{target('Figure 17.4', 'Students with an outcome outside the stated 400 to 1600 scale')} ",
    "of the {target('Figure 17.4', 'Students in total')} simulated students score outside 400 ",
    "to 1600. Both panels of Figure 17.4 set their limits at 400 and 1600, so those students ",
    "are clipped out of the published figure and a reader cannot see them. The clipping ",
    "changes only what is drawn: the classroom means and their intervals are computed from ",
    "all {target('Figure 17.4', 'Students in total')} students before plotting, and ",
    "`coord_cartesian()` zooms the axis without dropping any data, so no plotted estimate ",
    "moves. The clipping is the chapter's own choice about the figure; what is wrong is the ",
    "sentence's claim about the data."),
  "clustered_outcome_scale",
  NA_character_,

  3, "description", "pipeline", "full",
  "Figure 17.3b compares neighborhoods, not schools",
  "p. 328, Section 17.5.2",
  "By contrast, in Figure 17.3b, we facet by randomly assigned group, so we compare across [[schools]] and within treatment group.",
  "By contrast, in Figure 17.3b, we facet by randomly assigned group, so we compare across [[neighborhoods]] and within treatment group.",
  str_glue(
    "The blocked example has ",
    "{param('Figures 17.2 and 17.3', 'Number of neighborhoods')} neighborhoods, of ",
    "{param('Figures 17.2 and 17.3', 'N in neighborhood 1')} and ",
    "{param('Figures 17.2 and 17.3', 'N in neighborhood 2')} residents, and the horizontal ",
    "axis of the published Figure 17.3b is labelled \"Neighborhood 1\" and \"Neighborhood 2\". ",
    "There are no schools in this design. The chapter's classroom example is the ",
    "cluster-randomized experiment of Figure 17.4, two sections later."),
  "fig3b_across_schools",
  NA_character_,

  4, "label", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The vertical axis of Figure 17.5 misdescribes the raw outcome scale",
  "p. 330, Figure 17.5",
  "Outcome variable [[(raw scale is 7-point Likert)]]",
  str_glue("Outcome variable [[(raw scale is continuous, {en_range(param('Figure 17.5', 'Outcome range'))})]]"),
  str_glue(
    "The outcome plotted in the unadjusted facet takes ",
    "{param('Figure 17.5', 'Number of distinct outcome values')} distinct values across ",
    "{param('Figure 17.5', 'N')} units, running from ",
    "{param('Figure 17.5', 'Outcome range')}, and ",
    "{target('Figure 17.5', 'Units with an outcome outside the 1 to 7 range the axis label implies')} ",
    "of them fall outside the 1 to 7 range a seven-point item allows. The generator draws the ",
    "outcome as `Y ~ 0.5 * Z + 1.0 * X + 0.5 * Z * X + U` with a normal covariate and normal ",
    "disturbance, so nothing about it is an ordinal item; the facet's own axis runs from 0 to ",
    "10. The chapter's only Likert outcome is the attrition example in Figure 17.8, which is ",
    "genuinely seven-point. The deposited script writes this label, so the chapter printed ",
    "what its own code gave it. Nothing plotted in Figure 17.5 changes, and the figure is not ",
    "reprinted: the correction is to the axis title alone."),
  "fig5_axis_label_likert",
  NA_character_,

  5, "label", "reading", "brief",
  "The subcaption of Figure 17.4a is missing a space and does not say what sets the point size",
  "p. 330, Figure 17.4a",
  "Cluster means are [[plotted,with]] point size proportional to [[size]]",
  "Cluster means are [[plotted, with]] point size proportional to [[cluster size]]",
  "Each point in Figure 17.4a is a classroom's mean, drawn in proportion to the number of students in that classroom.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  6, "spelling", "reading", "brief",
  "A doubled \"from\"",
  "p. 321",
  "a population other than the one from which [[from]] the sample was drawn",
  "a population other than the one from which the sample was drawn",
  "",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  7, "spelling", "reading", "brief",
  "\"Simply\" for \"simple\"",
  "p. 332",
  "they rely on a relatively [[simply]] logic",
  "they rely on a relatively [[simple]] logic",
  "",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  8, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Sarah Khan's surname is misspelled, in the text and in the reference list",
  "pp. 326 and 336",
  "See, for example, [[Kahn]] (2017)\n\n[[Kahn]], Sarah. 2017.",
  "See, for example, [[Khan]] (2017)\n\n[[Khan]], Sarah. 2017.",
  "The author is Sarah Khan (PhD, Columbia University; now at Yale University), who presented the paper under the title cited. It is unpublished and has no DOI.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  9, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Bullock and Ha (2011) is given the wrong pages",
  "p. 335",
  "Cambridge University Press, [[p. 959]].",
  "Cambridge University Press, [[pp. 508--522]].",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1017/CBO9780511921452.035: the chapter runs from p. 508 to p. 522.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  10, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Both publishers of Bertin (1967) are misspelled",
  "p. 335",
  "Editions [[Gauthier-Villar]].\n\nReissued in 2010, [[Ersi Press]].",
  "Editions [[Gauthier-Villars]].\n\nReissued in 2010, [[Esri Press]].",
  "The first edition was published in Paris by Mouton and Gauthier-Villars, and the English translation was reissued by Esri Press (Redlands, CA).",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  11, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Lupi and Posavec (2016) is given the wrong publisher",
  "p. 336",
  "Dear Data. [[San Francisco, CA: Chronicle Books]].",
  "Dear Data. [[New York: Princeton Architectural Press]].",
  "Dear Data was published in the United States by Princeton Architectural Press, and in the United Kingdom by Particular Books.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  12, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "W. E. B. Du Bois Center (2018) is given the wrong publisher and loses the initials' full stops",
  "p. 336",
  "2018. [[WEB Du Bois's]] Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America. [[San Francisco, CA: Chronicle Books]].",
  "2018. [[W. E. B. Du Bois's]] Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America. [[New York: Princeton Architectural Press]].",
  "The book was published by Princeton Architectural Press in 2018, edited by Whitney Battle-Baptiste and Britt Rusert for the W. E. B. Du Bois Center at the University of Massachusetts Amherst.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  13, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Wilkinson's Grammar of Graphics is given the wrong year and place of publication",
  "pp. 323 and 336",
  "(Wilkinson [[2006]])\n\nWilkinson, Leland. [[2006]]. The Grammar of Graphics. [[Berlin: Springer Science+Business Media]].",
  "(Wilkinson [[2005]])\n\nWilkinson, Leland. [[2005]]. The Grammar of Graphics. [[New York: Springer]].",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1007/0-387-28695-0: the second edition, Springer New York, 2005.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  14, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Wickham (2016) is given the wrong place of publication",
  "p. 336",
  "Data Analysis. [[Berlin: Springer]].",
  "Data Analysis. [[Cham: Springer International Publishing]].",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1007/978-3-319-24277-4: Springer International Publishing, Cham.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  15, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Chambers et al. (1983) is given the wrong place and imprint",
  "p. 335",
  "[[Boston, MA: Wadsworth]].",
  "[[Belmont, CA: Wadsworth International Group]].",
  "The 1983 edition was published by Wadsworth International Group in Belmont, California (and by Duxbury Press in Boston).",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  16, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "Titiunik's given name loses its accent",
  "p. 336",
  "and [[Rocio]] Titiunik",
  "and [[Rocío]] Titiunik",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1017/S0003055416000575.",
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing, so it carries NA whatever its class. An empty claim_ids is stored
# as "" and counts as missing here.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
needs_value <- entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[!needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# Every id an entry claims to correct must be a real ground-truth claim. The build gate in
# ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R checks the same property from the other side; checking it
# here too means a dangling id cannot survive a render.
gt_ids <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "coppock_2021_ground_truth.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)$claim_id
cited_ids <- entries$claim_ids |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(x) is.na(x) | x == "")
stopifnot(all(cited_ids %in% gt_ids))

# The prose below counts the entries in words, as the note has always done.
n_entries_word <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
                    "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen",
                    "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")[nrow(entries)]

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# An entry that corrects more than one place carries one block per place, separated by a
# blank line; each stays inside the quotation.
quote <- function(x) str_replace_all(bold(x), "\n\n", "\n>\n> ")
```

This note lists `r n_entries_word` corrections to "Visualize as You Randomize: Design-Based Statistical Graphs for Randomized Experiments," chapter 17 of *Advances in Experimental Political Science* (Druckman and Green, eds., Cambridge University Press, 2021, pp. 320--336), doi [10.1017/9781108777919.022](https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108777919.022). **None of them changes a conclusion of the chapter**, which is a methodological argument about how to draw statistical graphs for randomized experiments and does not rest on any quantity below. Three are sentences that misdescribe the simulated data behind a figure, and one is a vertical axis label that misdescribes the outcome it plots. The rest are smaller: two typos in the text, a garbled subcaption, and nine errors in the reference list. Every figure in the chapter is correct as printed, and none is reprinted here.

All the data in the chapter are simulated, and the deposited datasets ([10.7910/DVN/VE6VSR](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/VE6VSR)) are what the figures are drawn from. Every number in a corrected sentence and in the notes below is computed from those datasets at the time this document is rendered. Bold marks what has changed. The code and output supporting each correction are in the actively maintained replication repository for this chapter, `active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2021`.

```{r entry-1, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every emitted entry opens
# with one.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 1)
cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
    "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r entries-2-3, results="asis"}
emit <- function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", quote(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", quote(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
walk(which(entries$entry %in% 2:3), emit)
```

```{r entry-4, results="asis"}
# This entry's published field is an axis label rather than a sentence, so it takes its own
# lead-in.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 4)
cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nThe vertical axis of Figure 17.5 is labelled:\n\n> ",
    bold(e$published), "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n",
    sep = "")
```

```{r remaining-entries, results="asis"}
walk(which(entries$entry >= 5), emit)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# carries these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
